newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan July overseas ship orders up 172 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan July overseas ship orders up 172 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Ship export contracts concluded by Japanese shipyards in July jumped 172 percent from a year earlier to 1.77 million gross registered tonnes (grt), representing 39 vessels, an industry body said on Tuesday.
The surge was partly due to brisk demand for very large crude carriers (VLCCs), a spokesman for the Japan Ship Exporters' Association said.
"Japan received only two VLCC orders in the three-month period from April to June, but we saw three VLCC contracts concluded last month," he said.
The orders for July also included 11 freighters, 17 bulk carriers, seven chemical tankers and one liquefied petroleum gas vessel, he said.
From January to July, Japan won orders for 194 vessels, or 7.42 million grt, while South Korea, another leading shipbuilder, received orders for 115 ships totalling 6.5 million grt, he added.
